claims.text: The starting MnNiSi-based alloy has a homogeneous matrix in its as-cast or as-rolled state.
A controlled heat treatment can induce a high volume fraction of coherent, ordered nanoprecipitates within a MnNiSi matrix.
Appropriate heat-treatment temperature, time, and cooling rate can promote nanoprecipitate nucleation and growth without coarsening or loss of coherency.
Heat-treatment conditions used in similar high-entropy alloys are analogous to conditions suitable for MnNiSi-based alloys.
The intervention will produce coherent, ordered nanoprecipitates with minimal lattice mismatch to the MnNiSi matrix.
Coherent, ordered nanoprecipitates increase mechanical strength.
High precipitate–matrix coherency minimizes lattice-distortion fields that affect magnetic domain-wall motion.
Minimizing interference with magnetic domain-wall motion prevents degradation of the magnetocaloric effect.
The treated MnNiSi-based alloy will have significantly greater yield strength and hardness than the untreated or standard-annealed baseline.
The treated alloy will retain a magnetocaloric effect comparable to that of the baseline material.
Standard annealing of the baseline does not induce a high volume fraction of coherent nanoprecipitates.
The beneficial combination of mechanical and magnetocaloric properties requires the nanoprecipitates to remain finely dispersed and coherent.
Excessive precipitate growth or loss of coherency may disrupt magnetic-domain behavior and reduce the magnetocaloric effect.
The optimal heat-treatment temperature, duration, and cooling rate are not yet known and may require fine-tuning.
